reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about ordering kinetics, phase boundary evolution, and their mechanistic link to embrittlement in AlCoCrFeNi2.1, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises.
premises: Thermal aging at ~600°C enhances L12 ordering in the FCC phase of AlCoCrFeNi2.1
Enhanced L12 ordering increases APBE and restricts dislocation cross-slip, promoting planar slip
Aging at ~600°C forms jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries
Planar slip and jagged boundaries cause local stress concentrations and brittle fracture
Aging at ~750°C reduces L12 ordering and forms ductile transition zones, restoring toughness
